themes.title: General-purpose humanoids
themes.description: Unitree's post-IPO honeymoon is over: shares slumped from their Aug 19 intraday peak of RMB 1,100 to the RMB 585-605 range by Aug 24-28, a roughly 45% decline that erased close to RMB 200B in market value and drew explicit bubble warnings from analysts, including Bank J. Safra Sarasin's Asia CIO, who called the valuation "probably not justified." Beijing's World Robot Conference and second World Humanoid Robot Games (Aug 19-23) put ~2,000 humanoids on display, with Tiangong Ultra (9.39s) and Honor's Lightning (~9.32-9.47s) both beating Usain Bolt's 100m world record of 9.58s. Tesla's Optimus remains unverified — Musk's July shareholder letter still describes lines "being installed" with output "anticipated later this year."

themes.title: Warehouse & logistics automation
themes.description: Symbotic's slide continued: Goldman Sachs cut its price target to $45 from $54 on Aug 25, the same week an SEC filing showed CTO James Kuffner sold roughly 3,952 shares (~$160K), and the stock closed near $40.41 — still digesting last week's dilutive share offering and Barclays' reaffirmed Sell rating despite a beat-and-raise Q3 print. A join-the-club moment (Stanford Robotics Center Industrial Affiliates Program) did little to offset the sentiment.

themes.title: Surgical robotics
themes.description: Intuitive Surgical unveiled a new manufacturing facility in Penang, Malaysia (Aug 20) to expand da Vinci 5 and My Intuitive+ capacity, and picked up reiterated Buy calls from BofA (Aug 11) and Citi ($685 PT, Aug 12). None of it has stopped the slide: shares are still down roughly 33% YTD, on pace for the weakest year since 2008, as J&J's Ottava now carries FDA de novo authorization for a full slate of soft-tissue procedures.

themes.title: Defense autonomy & drones
themes.description: AeroVironment's MacCready Works unit won a contract to co-design and co-manufacture three Mars helicopters for NASA's SkyFall mission, layered on top of a $51M Army order for Switchblade 600 Block 2 munitions and a $100M, 20-acre unified campus planned for Moorpark, CA. Kratos grew Q2 revenue 30.5% YoY with a $2.08B backlog. Yet both AVAV and KTOS shares have traded down in 2026 despite the contract wins — backlog growth and stock performance have decoupled this year.

themes.title: Field robotics
themes.description: Deere's autonomous articulated dump truck continues quarry operations under its 2nd-gen autonomy kit; Caterpillar's five-machine autonomous construction lineup remains in early rollout. Both stay diversified industrials where robotics is a small slice of the overall return — no fresh sector-specific news this week.

themes.title: Japanese factory automation
themes.description: Fanuc has given back some of its post-crash bounce, trading near ¥6,063 as of Aug 19 versus the ¥6,720 level seen the prior week — a reminder the recovery from the Aug 3 guidance shock is still choppy rather than a clean re-rating. Harmonic Drive Systems, a key humanoid-actuator supplier, sits at ¥5,910 (Aug 28) against a 7-buy/1-sell analyst consensus target of ¥7,731.

themes.title: Supply chain & components
themes.description: MP Materials extended its rally from $38 (Jul 29) to $60.05 (Aug 21) on a new gadolinium supply deal with a US aerospace/defense customer and accelerating 10X magnet-facility buildout; Morgan Stanley raised its price target to $73 (Overweight). A newer name worth tracking: Vishay Precision Group is now 2026's best-performing robotics supply-chain stock (+216% YTD, ahead of Ouster and Aeva), booking real humanoid-actuator orders on its strain gauges and load cells.

themes.title: The robot "brain"
themes.description: NVIDIA's Jetson Thor platform reached general availability (developer kit and production modules) on Aug 10, and the company's Aug 26 Q2 FY27 report showed why the compute layer still dominates the conversation: revenue of $96.22B (+5.7% above guidance), Data Center at $89B, and Q3 guidance of $108B. Adopters now span Agility, Amazon Robotics, Boston Dynamics, Caterpillar, Figure, Hexagon, Medtronic, Meta and China's Galbot.

themes.title: China scaling & listing
themes.description: Unitree's post-debut crash is now the sector's central China story — a ~45% slump inside a week that has reopened the "is this a bubble" debate for the whole 150+-company field. Elsewhere, Agibot says cumulative humanoid shipments have reached 15,000 units (up from 10,000 just weeks ago), and LimX Dynamics continues scaling its COSA operating system ahead of a planned Hong Kong listing.

bear_case.title: Unitree's crash is the bubble case made real
bear_case.description: Shares fell ~45% from their Aug 19 intraday peak to the Aug 24-28 close, erasing roughly RMB 200B in days. Bank J. Safra Sarasin's Asia CIO called the valuation "probably not justified," citing an "infant level" industry with intensifying competition. This is no longer a hypothetical bubble warning — it's a live repricing investors can watch happen.

bear_case.title: Humanoid funding still outruns humanoid revenue
bear_case.description: The median disclosed humanoid round between Aug 2025 and June 2026 was $145M, with rounds above $50M now 84% of all disclosed capital — most of these companies still don't have revenue that justifies the price tag. South Korea's Tomorrow Robotics went from ~30B won to a 450B won target valuation in under a year without a single confirmed commercial deployment.

bear_case.title: Demos ≠ autonomy
bear_case.description: If a humanoid demo isn't explicitly labeled autonomous, assume teleoperation. Dexterity, inference speed, reliability, and cost still confine real use to structured factory/warehouse tasks.

bear_case.title: Crowding & shakeout risk
bear_case.description: 150+ companies chasing humanoids, with Agibot alone now claiming 15,000 cumulative units shipped; a reshuffling of startups is widely expected. Robotics pioneer Rodney Brooks argues much of the investment will be wasted.

bear_case.title: Backlogs and beats don't protect the stock
bear_case.description: Symbotic got a fresh Goldman price-target cut (to $45 from $54) and an insider share sale this week — on top of last week's dilutive offering — despite real revenue growth. AeroVironment and Kratos both won new contracts this month, yet their shares have traded down in 2026 anyway. In parts of this sector, balance-sheet and sentiment signals are doing more work than headline numbers.

bear_case.title: Revenue is elsewhere
bear_case.description: Industrial, logistics, and surgical robots generate proven revenue today; humanoids largely don't yet. Component and warehouse names carry less thesis risk than humanoid pure-plays.

bear_case.title: China price war
bear_case.description: Unitree's $5,900 R1 signals aggressive price compression that could squeeze Western OEM margins before the market matures — and 150+ Chinese humanoid startups, now including BYD, are competing on price and scale even as Unitree's own stock struggles to hold its valuation.

bear_case.title: "Dot-com stage" warnings
bear_case.description: KB Securities likened 2026's robotics/space enthusiasm to the final stage of the dot-com bubble; Ray Dalio separately compared the broader AI bubble to 1929 and 2000 valuation extremes. Sector EV/EBITDA multiples ranged from 0.9x (mature industrials) to 78.2x (speculative pure-plays) in Q4 2025 — a valuation split investors should not treat as one trade.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Q2 FY27 revenue beat at $96.22B with Q3 guide of $108B, and Jetson Thor reached general availability Aug 10 with 2M+ developers already on the platform — the default compute layer keeps widening, not narrowing. Also your largest AI-sleeve holding and appears in your Quantum and Biotech sleeves too — don't triple-count the exposure.

positions.name: Rockwell Automation
positions.note: The cleanest listed US factory-automation exposure, benefiting from ~$200B in announced US factory buildouts, without a single-name dilution or guidance-shock risk like the ones that hit Symbotic and Fanuc this year.

positions.name: Teradyne
positions.note: Robotics segment's first-ever $100M quarter is holding up, and the stock is now +91% YTD on AI-test-equipment demand — sustained, diversified execution rather than a single make-or-break bet, though the size of the run argues for discipline rather than chasing it higher.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: New NASA Mars-helicopter contract, a fresh $51M Army order and a $100M Moorpark campus all landed this month, yet shares have still traded down in 2026 — a genuine disconnect between contract momentum and price that argues for staying sized rather than adding. Also sits in your Defense sleeve — size across both, not in each.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: Backlog grew to $2.08B on +30.5% YoY revenue growth, but negative cash flow and supply-chain issues persist — the same stock-vs-backlog disconnect as AeroVironment. Also counts against your Defense sleeve.

positions.name: Tesla
positions.note: Musk's July shareholder letter still describes Optimus lines as 'being installed,' with output now only 'anticipated later this year' — a further slip from the April timeline, more than a year into the Fremont conversion with zero verified units. Trimmed on continued delay.

positions.name: Harmonic Drive
positions.note: The Aug 19 Q1 FY2027 report struck a more cautious tone than the Aug 7 guidance raise, and shares have drifted to ¥5,910 against a ¥7,731 average target — the strain-wave-reducer bottleneck story still needs the humanoid order book to convert more consistently. Trimmed to fund a smaller, more diversified components basket.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Shares ran from $38 to $60.05 this month on a new gadolinium offtake deal and Morgan Stanley's $73 price target, but the company is still GAAP-loss-making as magnet-ramp costs bite. Also anchors your Critical Minerals sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Vishay Precision Group
positions.note: New this week: 2026's best-performing robotics supply-chain stock (+216% YTD) on real, booked humanoid-actuator orders for its strain gauges and load cells — small enough that customer concentration is a real risk, so sized accordingly.

positions.name: Symbotic
positions.note: Goldman cut its price target to $45 from $54 this week and an SEC filing showed the CTO selling shares — on top of last week's dilutive offering and Barclays' Sell rating. Real revenue growth isn't enough on its own to outweigh two straight weeks of negative signals; still on the sidelines.

positions.name: Cognex
positions.note: No fresh catalyst this week beyond last week's HSBC downgrade to Hold ($65 PT); the underlying machine-vision business still looks intact, but nothing has emerged yet to justify moving off the sidelines.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical

positions.name: Caterpillar

positions.name: Fanuc

positions.name: Unitree

positions.note: RPA is being disrupted by the same AI agents it claims to ride, and the robotics label is marketing rather than hardware.
